messages:
maria: Uploaded an nsys capture for the KV prefetch regression. link: https://redwood-nsys/reports/1876543210

maria: tl;dr — periodic stalls where kernels on stream 0 wait ~1.5-3ms while host->device memcpys on stream 4/5 occupy copy engine. I think CPU preemption of prefetch thread is correlated.

josh: which instance / driver?
maria: p4d.24xlarge, CUDA 12.2, driver 535.86, libcudnn 9.3. build: runtime-2026-02-15

kai: quick skim of the timeline: copy engine (~H2D) bursts every ~30ms, kernels spill over after the burst. Could be host scheduling + non-blocking flag missing.
anya: I pulled the thread slice. CPU shows prefetch_thread running, issues multiple cudaMemcpyAsync calls, then gets preempted by other OS work for ~2.4ms. When it resumes it queues more copies -> copy engine saturates -> kernels on default stream stall.

mike: can you paste the minimal snippet you saw?
maria: ```
[ 123.456 ms ] prefetch_thread: prepare batch, call cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src_pinned, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream=4)
[ 123.458 ms ] H2D memcpy (stream=4) duration=1.9 ms  <-- copy engine active
[ 125.358 ms ] kernel_forward (stream=0) attempts launch, BLOCKED by copy engine contention, wait 2.1 ms
[ 125.900 ms ] prefetch_thread CPU preempted (sched gap ~2.4 ms)
```

kai: two hypotheses:
- prefetch thread isn't pinned -> OS preemption causes bursts of copies when it resumes -> copy engine queueing
- copies are using pageable memory fallback (not actually pinned) causing implicit syncs and blocking kernels

josh: are copies using pinned buffers? build logs show allocator "hostpage_alloc" but not sure if pinned.

anya: I grep runtime logs: `prefetcher.allocate_host_slab(pinned=true)` in config, but older rollout didn't have that flag. Could be mixed.

mike: quick tests to run:
1) Force prefetcher to use pinned pages (set PREFETCH_PINNED=1) + restart
2) Set thread affinity: taskset -c 46,47 for prefetch thread
3) Run capture with CUPTI activity and `--trace=cpu,cuda,memory` and `--stats=true`

perf-bot: Auto summary: peak copy engine duty ~45%, average kernel wait time during bursts 1.8ms, CPU sched gaps correlate with 95% of those events. See report: https://redwood-nsys/reports/1876543210/summary

maria: I can run 1 & 2 now and post new capture. Any other flags we should try? maybe CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING? but that will change behavior.

kai: also try setting the prefetch thread to call `cudaSetDevice` and use a stream with `cudaStreamNonBlocking` semantics. But pinned + affinity first.

josh: also check whether copy stream uses `cudaMemcpyAsync` into device memory allocated in non-pooled allocator; pooled allocator fragmentation could force implicit syncs.

anya: if pinned + affinity removes gaps, we ship a hotfix to prefetcher to pin pages and set affinity on dedicated prefetch threads. If not, we look at batching to reduce copy frequency.

mike: +1. If you run captures, paste the new thread here.

maria: starting tests now, will post updated nsys in ~20m :thumbsup:
